pr_body:
Use a sync.Pool to reuse byte slices between calls to Marshal() in the remote read handler.

Fixes #11232.

Signed-off-by: Giedrius Statkevičius <giedrius.statkevicius@vinted.com>
pr_comments: Tried out with https://github.com/thanos-io/thanosbench that with this change I am able to retrieve ~33MiB in 5 seconds from Prometheus + Sidecar. Without this change, I am able to retrieve only ~31MiB in 5 seconds. So, only a small improvement but still an improvement nonetheless.

Added a small microbenchmark. Here is the diff:

```
name                   old time/op    new time/op    delta
StreamReadEndpoint-16    43.7µs ± 3%    39.9µs ± 3%  -8.70%  (p=0.004 n=5+6)

name                   old alloc/op   new alloc/op   delta
StreamReadEndpoint-16    28.8kB ± 0%    26.9kB ± 0%  -6.60%  (p=0.000 n=5+4)

name                   old allocs/op  new allocs/op  delta
StreamReadEndpoint-16       292 ± 0%       277 ± 0%  -5.14%  (p=0.002 n=6+6)
```

issue_context.title: remote read / performance: reuse buffer for marshaling
issue_context.body: Currently, remote read handler allocates a new buffer for each response: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/314aa45c2ced676d6a76d5ce9333a60faa331570/storage/remote/codec.go#L235-L240. We can re-use the buffers with a `sync.Pool` instead of allocating a new one each time.
comments:
Ideally, we start simpler with static buffers/types first before we move to sync.Pool, but can definitely improve a lot here.

Help wanted!
Could I work on with this? @bwplotka
